title: Weekly Markets Monitor - Pricing fiscal risk
gist: World Gold Council's weekly monitor argues fiscal risk is being priced again: French government bond term premiums hit their highest since the early 2000s amid budget turmoil, with sovereign-debt worries spreading across major economies. It links continued European and US gold ETF buying, despite recent price weakness, to these debt-sustainability concerns, against a backdrop of geopolitical tension, slowing growth, hawkish Fed minutes and a surprise RBI hike.

themes.theme: French bond stress and term premiums

insights.claim: French government bond term premiums have climbed to their highest level since the early 2000s as budget negotiations begin, after recent turmoil in France's bond market.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: Watch OAT-Bund spreads and French budget talks as a live fiscal-risk flashpoint in European rates.
insights.quote: French government bond term premiums have climbed to their highest level since the early 2000s
insights.locator: Recent turmoil in France’s bond market

insights.claim: Fiscal sustainability concerns are not unique to France: the World Gold Council sees worries over rising sovereign debt burdens growing across major economies, which it tracks via Bloomberg Economics term premiums (weekly data, Jan 2020 to Oct 2026).
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: Rising term premiums across developed markets argue for structurally higher long-end yields and demand for non-sovereign hedges.
insights.quote: France is not alone: concerns over rising sovereign debt burdens are growing across major economies
insights.locator: Chart of the week: Pricing fiscal risk

insights.claim: European and US investors have kept allocating to gold ETFs over recent months despite recent gold price weakness, which the World Gold Council links to growing debt-sustainability concerns and rising term premiums.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: Sticky Western ETF inflows during price dips suggest fiscal-risk hedging demand is supporting gold; track ETF flows against term premiums.
insights.quote: European and US investors have continued to allocate to gold ETFs over the past few months despite recent price weakness
insights.locator: Against this backdrop, European and US investors

themes.theme: US fiscal, growth and Fed signals

insights.claim: In the week to mid-October 2026, US fiscal and trade deficits widened, consumer sentiment weakened, and Fed meeting minutes were hawkish, combining slowing-growth signals with a still-tight policy stance.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: Widening twin deficits plus a hawkish Fed into weakening sentiment is a stagflation-tinged mix supportive of gold and bearish for long Treasuries.

insights.claim: Major global stock markets rose over the week while bond yields edged lower but remained elevated, oil prices stayed high and the US dollar edged up.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: Risk assets are shrugging off geopolitical and fiscal stress while yields stay elevated, leaving gold competing with a firmer dollar.
insights.locator: Major global stock markets rose over the week

insights.claim: Middle East tensions lifted energy prices while the US eased sanctions on Russian diesel, amid heightened geopolitical risk and signs of slowing global growth.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: Easing Russian diesel sanctions may partly offset Middle East-driven energy upside; watch distillate cracks.

insights.claim: The Reserve Bank of India raised rates by 25bps to 5.5%, its first hike in nearly four years.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: An RBI tightening pivot is notable for Indian rates, rupee and potentially domestic gold demand in a key consumer market.
insights.quote: the RBI raised rates by 25bps to 5.5%, its first hike in nearly four years

insights.claim: German activity slowed, UK services softened and China's holiday spending was uneven, pointing to broad-based growth softness across Europe and Asia.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: Softening growth outside the US raises the odds of easier policy in Europe and China, a backdrop historically supportive of gold.
